name: PostHog Skills
summary: Official PostHog Agent Skills marketplace for Claude Code, covering platform, team, community and .meta skills. MIT; GitHub still describes the repo as under construction.
description: Vendor-affiliated listing (PostHog). The PostHog/skills repository is MIT (Copyright (c) 2025), not archived, and has a documented Claude Code marketplace, but the GitHub repository description still says “PostHog skills (under construction)”. The pack is free to install; PostHog product usage is billed under PostHog's own plans and was not re-verified here. This skills entry does not set mcp_endpoint. Documented install: `/plugin marketplace add PostHog/skills`, then `/plugin install posthog-integration@posthog-skills`, `/plugin install posthog-feature-flags@posthog-skills`, or `/plugin install posthog-all@posthog-skills` (or `/plugin search posthog`). None were run. The repo tree also has plugin.json files under skills/posthog/error-tracking, llm-analytics, logs, and tools-and-features (plugin names posthog-error-tracking, posthog-llm-analytics, posthog-logs, and posthog-tools), in addition to the integration, feature-flags, and all plugins the README documents. The README does not document install commands for those extra plugins and may lag the tree; no additional install IDs are claimed here, and those plugin.json files were not installed. Individual skill directories can also be copied into `.claude/skills/`. The README groups the library as official PostHog platform skills (analytics integration, feature flags, error tracking, LLM analytics and more; generated by PostHog/context-mill and updated automatically on each release), team skills, community skills, and .meta skills for creating and managing skills. https://posthog.com/docs/ai/skills returned 404 on 2026-11-16, so it is not used as docs or a source. No signup or spend.

agent_access.notes: Public MIT marketplace. Documented Claude Code marketplace/plugin installs were not executed. Using the skills against a PostHog project needs a PostHog account and is billed by PostHog; no account or spend was used. The README documents three plugin installs, but the repo also has plugin.json under error-tracking, llm-analytics, logs, and tools-and-features; the README may lag the tree.
